title: The itinerary clock
brief: Read a starting hour and minute, then a duration in minutes. Print the arrival time on a 24-hour clock, wrapping after midnight.
output: arrival=HH:MM, using two digits for hour and minute.
hints: Convert the departure time into total minutes.
Add the duration and take remainder modulo 1440.
Use /60, %60, and printf %02d to format HH:MM.

title: The itinerary clock: days travelled
brief: Keep the 24-hour arrival time and also print the number of whole days elapsed since departure.
output: arrival=HH:MM days=D, where D counts midnight crossings.
hints: Keep the complete minute total before taking its remainder.
Whole days equal total / 1440.
Print days after the existing arrival time.

title: The Collatz trail
brief: From N, repeat: if even, divide by 2; otherwise multiply by 3 and add 1. Count how many operations are needed to reach 1. Use a loop.
hints: Use a while loop that stops when value == 1.
Test parity with value % 2.
Increment steps after each transformation.

title: Collatz trail: highest peak
brief: Keep the step count and also track the largest value reached during the entire Collatz sequence, including the start.
hints: Initialise peak to the starting number.
After each update, compare the new value against peak.
Print peak after the existing step count.

title: Draw a terminal tile
brief: Read width W and height H. Use nested loops to print H lines, each with exactly W '#' characters.
input: Two integers W and H in [1,8].
output: Exactly H lines of W '#' characters each.
hints: The outer loop controls the rows.
The inner loop prints W characters on each row.
Print a newline after each row.

title: Terminal tile: hollow center
brief: Print the same rectangle but replace every interior character with '.', keeping '#' for the four borders.
output: Exactly H lines: '#' on the border and '.' inside.
hints: Keep both loops and the newline.
A cell is on the border if row==0, col==0, row==H-1, or col==W-1.
Print '.' only when all four border conditions are false.

title: Repeated neighbor readings
brief: Store N readings in a 1D array and count adjacent pairs containing the same value. For 5 5 5, there are two equal neighbor pairs.
hints: Read N values into an array.
Compare each cell i with the previous one, starting at i=1.
Increment a counter when a[i] == a[i-1].

title: Repeated readings: longest streak
brief: Keep the adjacent-pair count and find the longest consecutive sequence of identical readings (at least 1).
hints: Use a current run length starting at 1.
On equality, increment the run; otherwise reset it to 1.
Keep the maximum run encountered.

title: Uppercase a username
brief: Read an alphanumeric token (max 30 characters) and change all lowercase ASCII letters to uppercase without using string.h.
input: One nonempty ASCII alphanumeric token of 1–30 characters.
hints: Use char text[31] and scanf("%30s", text).
Walk through the string until '\0'.
For 'a'..'z', subtract 'a' and add 'A'.

title: Username: invert letter case
brief: Instead, swap the case of every ASCII letter: lowercase becomes uppercase and uppercase becomes lowercase. Leave digits unchanged.
hints: Keep the lowercase conversion.
Also detect 'A'..'Z' and convert them to lowercase.
Use mutually exclusive if/else if cases so a converted letter is not converted again.
